description: Language-neutral route conformance fixture shared by the Go router (internal/messaging/router) and the TypeScript router. 'repairs' is the template table every Repair()-rendered tool error is built from; 'applicability' is the per-action input contract both routers validate against (permitted keys, required keys, and each key's declared type); 'cases' drives both routers and the Go JSON-Schema test. A case's 'conditions' carries the Umpire conditions the router derives from the caller, surface and resolved target; 'provider' supplies the fake provider's Resolve result ('resolved'), the runtime status its RunState reports ('state'), the expected arguments of the router-to-provider call ('request') and what the provider returns. 'schema': true marks a case the JSON Schema must also reject. The token {message_id} inside 'expect.message', 'expect.facts' and 'provider.request' is replaced with the message id the caller minted, because Tell and Ask mint their own id. Facts are pre-quoted: a template carries no literal quotes and every fact that should render quoted arrives quoted. 'peers_applicability' and 'peers_cases' are the avenor_peers twin of 'applicability' and 'cases'.

repairs.target_not_terminal: run {run_id} is {status}; wait for it to finish before resuming
repairs.not_resumable: run {run_id} is not resumable (status: {status}); resume only continues done, failed, or blocked runs
repairs.string_too_short: property {name} must be at least {min} characters
repairs.string_too_long: property {name} must be at most {max} characters
repairs.string_pattern: property {name} contains characters that are not allowed
repairs.peers_invalid_action: not a known action (list, rename, last)
repairs.control_reply_unsupported: control replies are not available on this surface: its provider cannot deliver them
repairs.refused_io: the provider could not read the requested run's state
